title: Enterprise AI Caching Architecture Selection: Semantic Cache vs. Provider Prompt Caching vs. Prefix KV Cache

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Exact-Match SHA-256 String Cache + Dynamic Timestamp at Top of System Prompt
tiers.architecture: Hashing the raw request JSON while placing `current_time` or `user_name` at the very beginning of the system prompt

tiers.tier: Tier 2: Naive Global Vector Semantic Cache (`Cosine Similarity > 0.88` Without Negation/Entity/ACL Guard)
tiers.architecture: Caching full LLM responses in a global Redis/vector store and returning cached answers whenever query embedding cosine > 0.88

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Cloud Provider Prompt Caching Only (`Azure OpenAI / Anthropic Prompt Caching`, No Gateway Semantic Cache)
tiers.architecture: Ordering static system prompt + tools first to get 50%–90% provider KV prefix discounts, but recalculating identical FAQ queries

tiers.tier: Tier 4: Two-Tier ACL-Scoped Semantic Cache (`Redis + Cross-Encoder Gate`) + Canonical Prefix-Ordered `KV Cache` (`Provider / SGLang Radix`)
tiers.architecture: L1 Gateway Semantic Cache (`ACL_Hash + Entity/Number Guard + Cosine > 0.96 + Reranker`) for FAQ hits (`18ms`) + L2 Canonical Static-First Prompt Ordering for `82%` KV Prefix Cache Hit Rate on misses

scenarios.scenario: Why Putting `current_date` or `user_id` on Line 1 of Your System Prompt Destroys 100% of KV Prefix Caching
scenarios.question: A developer starts the 12,000-token prompt with `System: Today is 2026-11-20 09:14:22. User: Alice.` followed by 10,000 tokens of static tool definitions and domain rules
scenarios.model_answer: KV Prefix Caching (`Azure OpenAI Prompt Caching`, `Anthropic cache_control`, `vLLM APC`, `SGLang RadixAttention`) matches token blocks strictly from **index 0 (left-to-right)**: a single changing token at the top invalidates all 12,000 subsequent tokens! Tier 4 enforces **Canonical Static-First Prompt Ordering (`[Static System Rules -> Static Tool Schemas -> Cached RAG Docs -> Dynamic User/Time Suffix]`)**, boosting KV prefix hit rate from `4.2%` to `82.0%`
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 places dynamic timestamps at token index 5, causing a 0% KV prefix cache hit rate and paying full price on 12,000 tokens every call ($182K/mo).

scenarios.scenario: The 'Semantic Cache Collision' Disaster (`2025 Q3 Revenue` vs. `2026 Q3 Revenue` Have 0.96 Cosine Similarity!)
scenarios.question: User A asks 'What was Acme Corp's Q3 2025 revenue?' and 2 minutes later User B asks 'What was Acme Corp's Q3 2026 revenue?'; dense embedding cosine similarity is 0.958
scenarios.model_answer: Never trust dense embedding cosine similarity alone for semantic caching! Tier 4 applies a **Deterministic Entity/Number/Negation Extractor + Cross-Encoder Verification (`score > 0.96`)**: if dates (`2025 != 2026`), SKUs, negations (`can` vs `cannot`), or currency symbols differ, force a cache miss to L2 Prefix KV Cache (`0.0%` semantic collision)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 naive vector semantic cache (`threshold = 0.88`) serves the 2025 revenue number for the 2026 query (`14.8%` wrong-answer collision rate)!

scenarios.scenario: Preventing Cross-Tenant / Cross-Role Data Leaks Through Shared Semantic Cache (`ACL-Partitioned Cache Key`)
scenarios.question: An HR Director queries 'What is the severance policy for VP layoffs?' (cached in Redis); 5 minutes later a junior contractor asks the same question
scenarios.model_answer: Partition all L1 Semantic Cache namespaces by `Cache_Partition_Key = SHA256(Tenant_ID + RBAC_Role_Set + Corpus_Version_Hash)`: a cache lookup only searches entries generated under an identical or subset ACL scope (`0.0%` cross-tenant/role cache poisoning)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 global semantic cache returns the HR Director's confidential answer to the contractor (`9.4%` cross-role leak).

scenarios.scenario: Combining L1 Gateway Semantic Cache (`Redis / APIM`) with L2 Engine Prefix KV Cache (`SGLang / vLLM / Cloud`)
scenarios.question: Which workloads belong in L1 Response Semantic Cache versus L2 Model-Level Prefix KV Cache?
scenarios.model_answer: Use L1 Gateway Semantic Cache only for **stateless single-turn FAQ / search queries** (`32%` hit rate at `18ms` latency, `100%` token savings); use L2 Prefix KV Cache for **multi-turn Agent loops, coding assistants, and RAG** where the query changes every turn but the 10K-token system/tool/history prefix stays constant (`78.4%` blended token cost reduction, `$41K/mo` TCO)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Using semantic response caching on multi-turn agent tool loops returns stale tool actions and breaks state transitions.

perturbation_checks.check: Antonym / Negation Perturbation (`'Is port 443 open?'` vs. `'Is port 443 closed?'` — 0.94 Cosine)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 0.0% Collision (Negation/Polarity Guard + Cross-Encoder Rejects L1 Hit & Routes to L2 KV Cache)

perturbation_checks.check: Underlying Knowledge Base Document Update (`Policy v2.4 Published`)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 0.0% Stale Answers (Event-Driven Cache Invalidation by `doc_chunk_id` Tag & `Corpus_Version_Hash`)

key_findings: Tier 4 (L1 ACL-Scoped Entity-Guarded Semantic Cache + L2 Canonical Static-First Prefix KV Cache) achieves 78.4% input token cost reduction, 195ms P95 TTFT, 0.0% semantic collisions, and $41K/mo TCO (-77.5% vs Tier 1).

Placing dynamic timestamps or user metadata at the top of a system prompt invalidates 100% of left-to-right KV Prefix Caching; enforcing Static-First Canonical Prompt Ordering unlocks 82% KV cache hit rates automatically.

Naive vector semantic caches (`cosine > 0.88`) suffer a 14.8% wrong-answer collision rate on dates, numbers, and negations (`2025` vs `2026`); semantic caches must enforce ACL partitioning, exact number/date matching, and cross-encoder verification.
